catalog_quote: [p. 216] All Bs speech varieties except some dialects of Kuy and Tsg retain phonemic accent. The following minimal pair is found in all dialects and establishes contrastive accent for PBS: púnuq [pú:nŭq] tree trunk < PBS *púnuq and punúq [pŭnúq] full < PBS *punúq. [p. 50] The vowel in an accented open penult (CV́) is long: all dialects (but Kuy and Tsg) bátaq → bá:taq young. The vowel in an unaccented (CV̆) or closed (CVC) syllable is short: all dialects manúk → mănúk chicken. Except for cases of compensatory lengthening, the vowel in the ultima is short ... In all dialects studied (except Kuy) stems or derivatives with a closed penult [CVC.CV(C)] are accented on the penult (see 10.2.1.). [p. 218] (1) CANONICAL FORM. In all Bs dialects studied, a closed penult is stressed. Thus, stress is predictable from the shape of the form: all dialects síŋsiŋ ring < PBS *síŋsiŋ, all dialects búkbuk weevil < PBS *búkbuk. Regardless of the accent on the base form, if morphophonemic changes produce a form with a CVC-penult, the penult is stressed. ... (3) ACCENT PAIRS of verb stems and their stative counterparts are found throughout Bs, e.g., most dialects tápus to finish: tapús finished; báyad to pay: bayád paid; ... Ban, Odg, Sib yútoq, Rom, Cap, Hil lútoq, Mas, War, Ceb, Sur, But lútuq: Ban, Odg, Sib yutóq, Rom, Cap, Hil lutóq, Mas, War, Ceb, Sur, But lutúq cooked

new_statements.rule_in_words: Capiznon, like all Bisayan dialects except Kuyonon and (Jolo) Tausug, has contrastive word accent on either the penult or the ultima (púnuq 'tree trunk' vs punúq 'full'; Cap lútoq 'cook' vs lutóq 'cooked'). An accented open penult is realised long; the ultima is never long. The one predictable case: a closed (CVC) penult is always accented (penultimate stress). Accent is partly morphologised (affix classes shift it, ch. 4.2).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not stated for Capiznon. Zorc's glossary defines secondary accent as antepenult length 'in some dialects'; sec. 10.2.3 p. 244 lists Cap among dialects with no long vowels in the antepenult.
new_statements.exceptions: Closed penult forces penult accent regardless of base accent; stress (as opposed to length) can shift under exclamatory intonation ('stress is a syntactic feature.. does not always coincide with length'); affixes may shift accent (penult-accent and ultima-accent affix classes).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level (stems and derivatives, citation forms); Zorc separates length (lexical/morphological) from stress (phrase/intonation-sensitive). Statement is family-level for the 36 sampled Bisayan dialects, with Capiznon explicitly in the sample and in the p. 218 accent-pair list.
new_statements.identity_note: Zorc 1977 'Capiznon (Cap)' = Capiz-area Bisayan of Panay, classed Central Bisayan next to Hiligaynon (Zorc's own field notebook, zorc.net, downloaded). Same variety as Glottolog capi1239 / ISO cps. Uy-Griño 2011 treats it as a subdialect of Hiligaynon (hili1240), whose held sketch (Zorc 2001) gives the same penult-or-ultima rule; Panit-an Capiznon (rural /l/ > /w, j/ lect) is a sub-dialect without its own glottocode. The stress statement is family-level for 36 Bisayan dialects, with Capiznon in the sample and in the lútoq : lutóq accent-pair list.

sources.note: Sec. 3.1.3 Accent p. 50: in all Bs dialects but Kuyonon and Tausug accent = length+stress; accented open penult is long (bá:taq), closed penult always accented; stress can be overridden by intonation. Sec. 8.10 p. 216: all Bs varieties except some Kuy/Tsg retain phonemic accent, minimal pair púnuq 'tree trunk' : punúq 'full' in all dialects. 8.10.2 p. 218: closed penult stressed; accent pairs verb:stative incl. 'Rom, Cap, Hil lútoq : lutóq cooked'. 10.2.1 p. 243: penultimate stress on inherited words with closed penult; 10.2.3 p. 244: Cap has no antepenult length.
